sections.h2: Per litre, E20 releases at most 6.8% less CO2 than petrol, not 30%

chart.title: Per-litre CO2 cut rises only to 10.2% at E30, so E20 gives 6.8%
chart.sub: CO2 cut per litre burned against pure petrol (E0), %.
chart.source: Author's calculation from standard combustion constants.

sections.means: Ethanol carries about 66% of petrol's carbon per litre, so each 5-point blend step trims CO2 by about 1.7%.
sections.todo: Ask for tested CO2-per-kilometre figures at each blend level before accepting any per-litre or headline cut.

sections.h2: Net CO2 per kilometre falls only where the engine is calibrated for E20

chart.title: Only an engine calibrated for E20 gets a real net CO2 cut per km
chart.sub: Net change in CO2 per kilometre driven at E20, %.
chart.source: Author's calculation; NITI Aayog roadmap (2021) mileage data.

sections.means: An uncalibrated engine loses about as much mileage as the fuel's energy gap, so its CO2 cut disappears.
sections.todo: Tie any E20 CO2 claim to the calibration status of the vehicles it is measured on.

sections.h2: Measured E20 mileage loss of 2–6% stays under the 6.8% ceiling

chart.title: Engine calibration recovers most of the energy loss, but cannot exceed it
chart.sub: Mileage loss at E20 against pure petrol, %.
chart.source: Lok Sabha reply, 30 July 2026; NITI Aayog roadmap (2021); author's calculation.

sections.means: No measured E20 mileage loss in India exceeds the energy-content ceiling of 6.8%.
sections.todo: Publish tested mileage at E25 and E30 before any blend above E20 is planned.
